findings.where: canvas in 'Patient Admissions Trend' and 'Department Distribution'
findings.evidence: dom-1440 elements 98 and 102 are <canvas> with no accessible name, no role="img", no fallback content and no data table; screen readers get nothing from either chart.
findings.after: <canvas role="img" aria-label="Admissions and discharges per day, Mon to Sun; admissions peak Thursday at 65"> plus a visually-hidden <table> of the daily values (and department counts for the donut)
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.1.1 Non-text Content and 1.3.1 Info and Relationships.

findings.where: Department Distribution donut and admissions chart legend
findings.evidence: Five departments are distinguished only by hue (blue, green, orange, violet, grey) with no values or direct labels on segments; Admissions vs Discharges only by blue vs green line.
findings.after: Direct labels with counts on or beside each segment/line end, or replace with labelled bars

findings.evidence: Three plain <button>s acting as a single-select toggle; no aria-pressed or tab roles captured (role: null). The selected period is shown only by fill colour (missing in this render).
findings.after: <div role="group" aria-label="Chart period"> with aria-pressed="true" on the active button (or a radiogroup), and a non-colour selected cue (weight or underline)
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value and 1.4.1 Use of Color.

findings.evidence: Accessible name is "Notifications" while the visible badge reads "3" (focus.json text "3"); the unread count is either dropped from the name or read as a bare '3'.
findings.after: <button aria-label="Notifications, 3 unread"> and aria-hidden on the visual badge
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 4.1.2 Name, Role, Value and 2.5.3 Label in Name.

findings.evidence: The only h1 is the product wordmark in the sidebar; the page's own title is an h2, and the KPI cards have no heading. Heading navigation starts at the logo.
findings.after: Make the wordmark a link or plain text and set 'Healthcare Analytics' (or the page's real title) as the h1; add a visually-hidden h2 'Key metrics' over the KPI row
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.3.1 Info and Relationships and 2.4.6 Headings and Labels.

findings.evidence: All five nav links have href="#" and none carries aria-current="page"; 'Dashboard' is the current page only by darker text colour.
findings.after: Dashboard with a non-colour current marker
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 2.4.4 Link Purpose and 1.4.1 Use of Color; 4.1.2 for current state.

findings.evidence: Field has an accessible name but name="", type="text", and the placeholder carries the instruction 'Search patients...' (A11-144).
findings.after: <form role="search"><label class="sr-only" for="q">Search patients</label><input id="q" name="q" type="search" placeholder="Name or patient ID"></form>

findings.evidence: Each row's first cell reads avatar initials then name ("JD John Doe john.doe@email.com"), so a screen reader announces the initials as a word before every name.
findings.why: WCAG 2.2 1.3.1 Info and Relationships (decorative duplicate content).

strengths: Landmarks present (nav, header, main); table uses real th headers.
Focus order follows visual order: sidebar links, search, notifications, period buttons, View All; nothing is covered.
not_investigated: disputed: A11-001 'Weekly' 1.00:1 is a capture artefact: tailwind.config was ignored by the shim so the active button's primary fill is missing; re-check with the real build
status pill colours (Recovered / In Treatment / Scheduled) could not be judged for colour-only meaning because their fills were lost in the shim
keyboard operation of charts and View All: no live run
